title: MelloHunt

thumb.alt: MelloHunt campaign key art featuring Marshmello

role: I co-led MelloHunt with Markel Lee as AOE Creative's CTO. I owned the project plan, the production pipeline across creative, social and creator teams, and the mechanics behind the hunt itself, from how clues were hidden to how entries were judged and rewarded.
task: Transform Lenovo Legion from trusted gaming hardware into a more culturally relevant brand through its first major celebrity partnership.

heading: Beyond
Performance
challenge.body: Gamers already trusted Legion for performance. What it lacked was cultural pull with Gen Z. This was Legion's first big celebrity partnership, and we didn't want it to read like another product endorsement. Legion had to show up naturally inside Marshmello's world of gaming, music and touring.

image.alt: MelloHunt wallpaper artwork with Marshmello and Legion branding

heading: Finding
the Crossover
bullets: Identified the intersection between Marshmello's music career, gaming credibility, and Legion's audience.
Developed Game Face On Tour as lifestyle storytelling rather than a traditional product demonstration.
Integrated Legion hardware naturally into Marshmello's gaming and music-production routine.
Built MelloHunt around the content, turning passive viewing into an interactive product discovery game.
Extended the activation across TikTok and Instagram to leverage Marshmello's audience and encourage participation.

blocks.label: Cultural Partnership
blocks.body: Connected Legion with Marshmello to bridge gaming, music, entertainment, and Gen Z culture.

blocks.label: Tour Storytelling
blocks.body: Game Face On Tour gave fans behind-the-scenes access while naturally positioning Legion within Marshmello's everyday routine.

blocks.label: Platform Boost
blocks.body: The campaign premiered through Marshmello's TikTok and Instagram presence to immediately reach a massive gaming-adjacent audience.

blocks.label: Brand Evolution
blocks.body: The partnership helped move Legion beyond product performance toward a broader cultural position within gaming.

blocks.label: Gamified Content
blocks.body: MelloHunt challenged viewers to identify Legion and AMD moments hidden throughout the content.

blocks.label: Fan Rewards
blocks.body: Fans who correctly completed the hunt competed for Legion hardware and exclusive Marshmello merchandise.

title: Just Go

thumb.alt: Brian Baumgartner holding a Legion Go S beside a pixel-art bird

role: Markel and I co-led the Legion Go S launch. As CTO I ran product and project management: the production schedule, talent and creator logistics, and the social rollout that took the campaign from one hero film to a full launch.
task: Launch the Legion Go S without falling into the predictable performance claims and visual clichés dominating gaming hardware advertising.

heading: Avoiding
Clichés
challenge.body: Hardware ads had become a formula: specs, dramatic lighting, big performance claims. Competing on the same terms would have made Legion Go S invisible. We decided to make the ads people remembered by poking fun at the category instead.

image.alt: Legion Go S handheld key visual

heading: Embracing
the Unexpected
bullets: Identified overused gaming-ad tropes as the campaign's creative opportunity.
Cast Brian Baumgartner as an unexpected, culturally recognizable lead.
Developed a deliberately deconstructed commercial that broke the fourth wall.
Extended the narrative beyond the hero film through a rogue product giveaway.
Invited creators from different gaming and entertainment communities to reinterpret the concept.

image.alt: Fan comments reacting to the Just Go campaign

blocks.label: Self-Aware Ad
blocks.body: Brian moved between exaggerated gaming archetypes while openly exposing the conventions of gaming hardware commercials.

blocks.label: Creator Parodies
blocks.body: Supercatkei, Mande, and Merrick Hanna reinterpreted the concept through their own communities and creative styles.

blocks.label: Rogue Giveaway
blocks.body: Brian "stole" Legion Go S units from set and traded them to fans for SteamOS recommendations.

blocks.label: Unexpected Talent
blocks.body: Casting Brian Baumgartner gave the campaign comedic credibility and opened Legion to audiences beyond traditional gaming influencers.

blocks.label: Audience Expansion
blocks.body: The campaign presented the handheld through cozy, competitive, and first-time gaming perspectives.

blocks.label: Platform Storytelling
blocks.body: Hero content, creator extensions, and community interaction allowed one creative idea to evolve across multiple formats.

task: Turn Legion's EWC PC partnership into seven weeks of culturally relevant content that demonstrated how the brand empowers every level of gamers.

heading: More Than
A Sponsorship
challenge.body: Being official PC partner bought visibility. Visibility alone doesn't keep people watching for seven weeks. We had to give gamers a reason to keep coming back to Legion while juggling products, creators, live competition and dozens of game communities at once.

heading: Building the

bullets: Built a seven-week content ecosystem rather than treating EWC as a single event.
Partnered with 11 creators representing different games, audiences, and creator styles.
Developed recurring formats spanning short-form, long-form, live streams, challenges, and fan participation.
Connected digital storytelling with physical EWC experiences and Legion products.
Designed activations that rewarded both creator competition and community participation.

title: Reel Rumble

thumb.alt: The three Reel Rumble creator captains

role: I co-led Reel Rumble with Markel. As CTO I designed how the competition worked, from the format and rules to voting and the prize flow, and managed the three creator teams through production.
task: Turn three separate creator communities into one participatory campaign that built Legion and AMD brand awareness through creativity rather than traditional product promotion.

heading: Creator
Competition
challenge.body: Creator deals easily turn into passive endorsements. Legion and AMD wanted fans to actually do something. We needed three separate creator communities to compete, make things and decide the winner together.

heading: Fan
Takeover
bullets: Partnered with CouRage, DrLupo, and HappyHappyGal around their established communities.
Built a competition around a behavior gaming audiences already understand: frag-reel editing.
Asked fans to transform creator Twitch footage into original short-form edits.
Centralized submissions through #ReelRumble on Instagram.
Used creator livestreams to review finalists and turn judging into content.
Shifted the final decision to fans through public likes and comments.

image.alt: The three Reel Rumble creator captains

blocks.label: Creator Captains
blocks.body: Three established creators rallied their individual communities around one shared competition.

blocks.label: Fan Editors
blocks.body: Participants transformed existing Twitch gameplay into original high-impact frag reels.

blocks.label: Live Judging
blocks.body: Creators reviewed submissions on stream, extending participation beyond the original posts.

blocks.label: Public Finals
blocks.body: One finalist from each community advanced to a social vote decided by fans.

blocks.label: Community Rivalry
blocks.body: The format turned creator fandom into friendly competition while keeping Legion and AMD at its center.

blocks.label: Real Stakes
blocks.body: $40,000 in prizes provided meaningful incentive for creators and fans to participate.

title: Unreal Fest Chicago

thumb.alt: Legion mascot reflected in Chicago's Cloud Gate sculpture

role: Markel and I co-led Legion's Unreal Fest presence. As CTO I owned the booth experience plan, the hands-on demo flow for the Legion 9i, and the schedule that gave developers a reason to come back more than once.
task: Introduce the Legion 9i to professional game creators by turning a trade-show booth into a destination for creating, learning, experimenting, and connecting.

heading: Epic
Activation
challenge.body: Unreal Fest is a room full of developers and technical artists. They know hardware. Telling them the 9i was powerful wouldn't work. We had to let them prove it to themselves, and make a small booth worth revisiting all week.

image.alt: The Legion booth at Unreal Fest Chicago

heading: Create
Experience
Connect
bullets: Built the experience around three behaviors: Create, Experience, Connect.
Designed programming for different levels of attendee involvement.
Combined hands-on hardware demonstrations with education and entertainment.
Partnered with respected game creators and Unreal Engine specialists.
Gamified repeat booth visits through a physical participation system.
Connected on-site programming to social content that extended the experience beyond Chicago.

blocks.label: Stamp Quest
blocks.body: A gamified booth journey rewarded attendees for exploring multiple experiences with exclusive Legion merchandise.

blocks.label: Creator Talks
blocks.body: Loftia and Exis Games demonstrated real game-development workflows using Legion hardware.

blocks.label: Live Creation
blocks.body: Neoliptus showcased Unreal Engine workflows live on the Legion 9i.

blocks.label: Product Demos
blocks.body: Legion specialists guided attendees through practical demonstrations focused on professional creative workflows.

blocks.label: Industry Voices
blocks.body: Scheduled conversations with Unreal developers explored the future of gaming and development.

blocks.label: Creative Hub
blocks.body: Programming transformed the booth from a product display into a place attendees could learn, create, and exchange ideas.

title: EMEA Championships

thumb.alt: League of Legends EMEA Championship artwork

role: I co-led the EMEA Championships experience with Markel. As CTO I was the bridge between Riot, our creative team and the developers, scoping what could ship, running the build and holding the quality bar to Riot's standard.
task: Create an interactive digital championship experience that met Riot's visual standards while coordinating the competing creative, technical, and operational requirements of three teams.

heading: Connecting
the Regions
challenge.body: Riot's visual bar was high, but the harder problem was alignment. Riot, our designers and the dev team all came in with different priorities. My job was to keep the experience ambitious without promising interactions we couldn't ship, and without letting tech limits water down the design.

heading: Designing
the Journey
bullets: Translated Riot's objectives into actionable creative and UX requirements.
Developed the experience architecture alongside visual exploration.
Designed the interactive EMEA map and supporting digital components.
Worked directly with developers to evaluate feasibility throughout design.
Managed Riot feedback while protecting consistency across the overall system.

gallery.alt: Interactive map of the EMEA region

blocks.label: Interactive Map
blocks.body: Fans could explore the EMEA region geographically and discover the leagues and stories connected to individual locations.

blocks.label: Regional Stories
blocks.body: The experience turned a large competitive ecosystem into accessible, location-driven storytelling.

blocks.label: Design Bridge
blocks.body: I acted as the creative connection between Riot stakeholders, designers, and developers throughout production.

blocks.label: UX Direction
blocks.body: Complex championship information was organized into a clear digital experience designed around fan exploration.

blocks.label: Technical Alignment
blocks.body: Engineering feasibility was considered throughout design rather than waiting until handoff.

blocks.label: Riot Standard
blocks.body: The final experience maintained the level of polish expected from one of gaming's most design-conscious publishers.

title: Immortal: Gates of Pyre

thumb.alt: Immortal: Gates of Pyre battle scene key art

role: Markel and I co-led Immortal: Gates of Pyre for Sunspear Games. As CTO I produced the UI, managed the Kickstarter campaign end to end, ran video production and built the website, while we shaped the identity system together.
task: Build a scalable identity and interface system for a completely new fantasy RTS IP with no existing visual equity or audience recognition.

heading: Lore
Genesis
challenge.body: A new IP starts with nobody knowing it exists. Immortal needed an identity that made an unfamiliar world feel real on day one, and that could flex across factions, lore, marketing, UI and a game still being built.

image.alt: Immortal: Gates of Pyre brand artwork

heading: Building
the World
bullets: Established the foundational visual language for the new IP.
Developed systems capable of connecting distinct factions under one master identity.
Worked directly with developers and artists to bridge visual ambition and technical feasibility.
Extended the identity into game UI so branding and interaction felt like one continuous system.
Iterated alongside the evolving game rather than treating branding as a static deliverable.

blocks.label: World Building
blocks.body: Brand elements were designed as artifacts of the universe rather than graphics simply placed on top of it.

blocks.label: Unified Identity
blocks.body: A scalable system connected multiple factions and visual environments without flattening their individuality.

blocks.label: Original Language
blocks.body: Created a complete custom glyph system that gave the fictional universe its own recognizable written language.

blocks.label: Game Interface
blocks.body: UI/UX extended the identity directly into the player's competitive experience.

blocks.label: Developer Collaboration
blocks.body: Design decisions were developed alongside programmers and artists so visual ambition remained technically achievable.

blocks.label: Living System
blocks.body: The brand was built to evolve alongside an unfinished game rather than solve only its immediate launch needs.

image.alt: Immortal: Gates of Pyre key art

title: Players on Paramount+

thumb.alt: The cast of Players in Fugitive team jerseys

role: I co-led the Fugitive branding for Paramount+ and Funny or Die's PLAYERS with Markel. As CTO I ran the fast-turnaround schedule and the research into how real League of Legends team brands evolved, then managed design through logos, jerseys and merch.
task: Create an esports organization that never existed and give it enough visual history to convince knowledgeable League of Legends fans that it had.

heading: Believable
Fiction
challenge.body: The show only worked if the team felt real. Fugitive couldn't look like a TV prop. It had to look like an org that had competed for years and lived through every awkward era of esports branding. We weren't designing one logo. We were designing a history.

heading: Designing
Backwards
bullets: Researched the evolution and visual conventions of League of Legends esports organizations.
Reverse-engineered the aesthetics and limitations of earlier esports branding.
Designed both contemporary and deliberately dated generations of Fugitive's identity.
Created historical visual artifacts that suggested years of fictional competition.
Extended the identity into jerseys, apparel, and production assets used throughout the series.

blocks.label: Fictional History
blocks.body: Rather than creating one identity, we designed multiple eras of Fugitive branding to establish believable organizational history.

blocks.label: Era Research
blocks.body: Early esports conventions were studied and intentionally recreated instead of simply distressing a modern logo.

blocks.label: Modern Identity
blocks.body: Fugitive's current identity needed to feel credible alongside real professional League of Legends organizations.

blocks.label: Legacy Marks
blocks.body: Older logo iterations created visual evidence of a team that had supposedly evolved over years of competition.

blocks.label: Authentic Merch
blocks.body: Jerseys and apparel extended the fiction beyond graphics and onto the characters themselves.

blocks.label: Invisible Design
blocks.body: The branding worked because it supported the story without calling attention to the fact that an entire competitive history had been fabricated.

title: Overwatch League

thumb.alt: Black, white and orange Overwatch League illustration

task: Build and evolve a global esports social presence that captured the energy of live competition.

heading: Hero
Inspired
challenge.body: OWL launched in 2018 as the first truly global esports league, and it needed a consistent brand across events, social and community. Then 2020 shut down live events. We had to pivot to digital-first overnight without losing fan excitement or sponsor value.

heading: Building
a League
bullets: Developed a comprehensive social media strategy tailored to each stage of the season (launch, weekly matches, playoffs, finals).
Built flexible creative systems that could scale from live-event marketing to fully digital engagement.
Directed illustration, graphic design, and content creation pipelines to support multiple teams, matches, and time zones each week.
Established community-driven activations that encouraged fans to contribute art, memes, and predictions, fostering a sense of ownership and identity.
Collaborated with internal Blizzard teams and external partners to ensure seamless execution across platforms.

Together

Built concepts inspired by gaming's shared experiences of “bringing people together”, from in-game items like Apex Legends' healing drone to nostalgic arcade machines.

task: Modernize LEGO's gaming identity with a new logo and visual system that reflects modern gaming culture while staying true to LEGO's DNA of play.

heading: Brick
by Brick
challenge.body: LEGO is a household name, but that doesn't carry over to gaming on its own. As LEGO went deeper into games, it needed an identity that could stand next to the biggest names in gaming and still feel like LEGO play.

heading: Connecting
Blocks
bullets: Collaborated with LEGO stakeholders to define brand architecture and positioning within the larger LEGO Group.
Explored multiple creative directions before aligning on a design that balanced modern gaming aesthetics with LEGO's playful DNA.
Built a comprehensive brand style guide to ensure consistent application across motion, digital, and promotional content.

blocks.label: Brand Identity
blocks.body: Designed the official LEGO Games logo and brand identity system.

blocks.label: Design Assets
blocks.body: Created supporting motion design and graphic assets to showcase the brand in digital-first environments.

blocks.label: Style Guide
blocks.body: Delivered a full brand toolkit and guidelines to empower LEGO's internal teams for future growth.

heading: Built
to Last
notes: Successfully launched a refreshed LEGO Games identity that aligned with the brand's future-facing ambitions.
Expanded LEGO's footprint in the gaming space with a modern, flexible identity system.
Provided creative assets that continue to support LEGO Games' presence in public campaigns and media.

title: Metal Umbrella
role: Markel and I co-led Metal Umbrella from the ground floor. As CTO I managed everything from naming and logo work through product design and the go-to-market plan for SypherPK's launch drops.
task: Launch SypherPK's fashion-first streetwear brand, building an identity that transcends streamer merch to stand as a lifestyle label.

heading: Too Young
Too Worry
challenge.body: Creator merch has a reputation for being low quality. SypherPK wanted a real fashion brand rooted in anime and gaming, with streetwear credibility, that could eventually stand without him. That meant a full identity system and product line, not a logo on a hoodie.

heading: Strategy
and Mechanics
bullets: Defined brand architecture and ethos: digital-native, anime/gaming inspired, fashion-first.
Developed the logo, identity system, and style guide to establish a recognizable aesthetic.
Directed creative for apparel design, packaging, and promotional content, ensuring consistency across touchpoints.
Built influencer marketing strategy, leveraging SypherPK's platform and community to amplify launch.

blocks.label: Brand Identity
blocks.body: Logo, identity system and style guide.

blocks.label: Apparel & Packaging
blocks.body: Directed design for the launch collections and packaging.

blocks.label: Influencer Launch
blocks.body: Built the launch strategy around SypherPK's platform and community.

heading: Victory
is Built
notes: Sold out first and second drops within the first month.
Elevated Metal Umbrella into a standalone lifestyle brand embraced by the streaming and fashion community.
